career.text: You need to learn a new tool for an assignment due in two days. What's your approach?

options.text: Follow the official quick-start, build a small sample, then apply it
Watch a long tutorial series before touching anything
Ask a friend to handle that part

career.text: A bug shows up in production but not on your machine. What do you do first?

options.text: Add print statements and redeploy until something shows up
Reproduce it with production-like settings and read the logs
Change code at random until it disappears

career.text: Your team misses an internal deadline. What do you do?

options.text: Work extra alone and say nothing
Wait for the mentor to decide what happens next
Call a quick check-in, agree a new plan and share it

career.text: You present your project to 50 people tomorrow. How do you prepare?

options.text: Outline key points, rehearse aloud twice and time it
Read the slides word for word

career.text: Two people finish a task in 6 hours at the same pace. How long would three people take?

assessment.title: Data Structures and Algorithms Quiz
instructions: This test contains 10 multiple choice questions.
You have 15 minutes to complete it. The test submits itself when time runs out.
You can flag questions and come back to them before you submit.
Once submitted, you cannot change your answers.

questions.text: Which data structure follows the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle?
What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
Which sorting algorithm guarantees O(n log n) time even in the worst case?
An inorder traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in what order?
Which data structure is normally used to implement breadth-first search?
What is the average time to look up a key in a hash table with a good hash function?
What is the space complexity of a recursive factorial function for input n?
Which technique finds a cycle in a linked list using constant extra space?
On an empty stack you push 1, push 2, pop, push 3, pop. What value did the last pop return?
A queue holds [1, 2, 3] with 1 at the front. After one dequeue and then enqueue(4), which element is at the front?
